reasoning: The remaining steps — git push to the public remote and gh release create — put the tag and artifacts in front of strangers and cannot be taken back cleanly once it lands. The skill's closing rule says a shown result closes the work, but it explicitly carves out that this changes nothing about the rule that a genuinely irreversible action still stops for his word before it runs, never only after it is shown. This is not one of the three taste-call cases — the work itself is verified and correct — it is instead a case where the action's irreversibility itself is the reason to stop before executing. The person has said nothing about this release since accepting the work, so the Director holds at the push/release boundary and speaks to the person first.
